title: Polonaise in A-flat major, Op. 53 “Heroic”
description: Chopin grew up in Warsaw and left at 20, never to return. His heart did: his sister smuggled it home, and it rests in a pillar of Holy Cross Church. This stirring polonaise, a Polish court dance, became a wartime emblem of national pride.

title: Halka: Mazur
description: Halka, by composer Stanisław Moniuszko, is the founding Polish national opera: a highland girl seduced and abandoned by a nobleman. Its full version premiered in Warsaw’s Grand Theatre in 1858; his statue stands outside. The mazur is a quick Polish dance.

title: Ta ostatnia niedziela
description: “This Last Sunday,” Jerzy Petersburski’s tango of a final farewell, was a 1935 hit for Warsaw crooner Mieczysław Fogg. Petersburski led a band at the Adria, the interwar city’s smartest dance hall; Fogg later sang for fighters in the 1944 uprising.

title: Kattorna
description: Pianist Krzysztof Komeda, who scored Roman Polanski’s early films, recorded his album Astigmatic at the National Philharmonic hall in December 1965. Often called the high point of Polish jazz, it opens with this theme from a Danish film.

title: Sen o Warszawie
description: “A Dream of Warsaw”: singer Czesław Niemen’s soaring song of longing to return to the city. Fans of Legia, Warsaw’s main football club, adopted it as their anthem and sing it en masse at the club’s stadium on Łazienkowska street.

title: Warszawa
description: In 1976 David Bowie’s train stopped at Warszawa Gdańska station and he walked the grey streets nearby, buying records of Polish folk music. The wordless chant he sang with Brian Eno on the album Low borrows from one of those folk songs.

title: Mniej niż zero
place: Polish Radio Three building, Myśliwiecka street
description: “Less Than Zero” made Warsaw band Lady Pank, led by guitarist Jan Borysewicz, stars under martial law. It topped the weekly chart of Polish Radio Three, the station that gave a generation its rock, broadcast from this building on Myśliwiecka street.

title: Ballade No. 1 in G minor, Op. 23 (The Pianist)
description: Pianist Janusz Olejniczak played the Chopin heard in Roman Polanski’s The Pianist. Władysław Szpilman, a Jewish pianist who escaped the Warsaw Ghetto, survived hiding in a ruined house at Niepodległości avenue 223, where a German officer found him.

title: Ukryty w mieście krzyk
description: “A Cry Hidden in the City,” from rapper Pezet and producer Noon’s album Muzyka klasyczna, is a moody night drive through Warsaw. Pezet came up in Ursynów, the vast 1970s concrete housing district on the southern edge of the city that bred its rap scene.

title: Godzina W
description: “W-Hour” was 5 pm on 1 August 1944, when the Home Army began the Warsaw Uprising, a 63-day revolt against German occupation. Rock band Lao Che made a whole album about it, launched at the Warsaw Rising Museum, which hosts their anniversary concerts.

title: Następna stacja
description: “Next Station,” from Warsaw rapper Taco Hemingway’s EP Umowa o dzieło, borrows the metro announcer’s phrase for a ride across a city of hustle and fatigue. Świętokrzyska is the downtown station where the two Warsaw metro lines meet.

title: Patointeligencja
place: Stefan Batory High School, Myśliwiecka street
description: The title is slang for “pathological intelligentsia”: Mata, a 19-year-old pupil at the elite Stefan Batory High School, rapped about rich Warsaw teenagers’ drugs and boredom. The song set off a national row and topped the Polish charts.

title: Szampan
description: “Champagne,” a breezy hit by Warsaw-born singer Sanah (Zuzanna Grabowska), a classically trained violinist. On 22 September 2023 she became the first Polish woman to sell out the National Stadium, the bowl-shaped arena on the Vistula’s east bank.
